segments.text: Hello Daniel, come in, have a seat. Where would you like to start today?
I don't really know. My general practitioner suggested I come.
She said I look exhausted and she's right, I am.
What does exhausted look like for you?
Like I'm running on fumes. I work as a project manager at a logistics company and I've been completely burnt out since October.
Since October? Did something happen then?
Not one thing. We lost a big client after the team Gov moved onto the rescue plan. So I ended up doing three people's jobs. Just never came back after that.
What does a normal working day look for you now?
I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 that night.
Even when I'm not working, I'm thinking about work.
That's a very long day. How's your sleep?
terrible, most nights I sleep about 4 hours, I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep
what happens when you wake at 3?
my head just hurts, shipping schedules, the client, whether I've forgotten something
Then I look at the clock and I do the math on how little sleep I'm gonna get, which makes it worse.
And then?
Then I lie until about five and get up and make tea.
I started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.
That sounds draining. Is there anything else going on in your life besides work?
Yeah, my father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
That's a lot to carry alongside everything else. How is he?
Still himself, mostly. His hands shake, he's slower, he gets frustrated.
He's having a dream and he's always been the strong one.
And how are you involved in his care?
I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds.
Neurology appointments are every few weeks. It's about an hour each way.
Is there anybody who shares that with you?
Not really. My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto, so all the care for our father falls on me.
How do you feel about that?
Guilty for even saying it. She calls him every Sunday. She's not the one who's neglecting him.
just I'm the one who's hearing.
Can you say more about the guilt?
He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.
So I don't say anything to anyone.
Not to Hana either?
She asks how I am and I say fine.
What would be the point? She can't do anything from Canada.
What would you want her to know if you said it?
That I'm not fine.
That someday I stay in a car park at a hospital for ten minutes before I go in.
Because I can't face it.
That's an important thing to notice.
What happens in those ten minutes?
Nothing really, just breathe. Look at every people going in.
Everybody looks tired here.
You mentioned your GP. What did she say?
She had blood tests.
They were all normal.
She said it's stress and exhaustion. If I asked about talking to someone,
they said I hadn't got the time.
And yet...
You are here.
My girlfriend booked that, to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.
How is it with Claire?
She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.
But I can see she's worrying about her too.
In what way?
She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.
Well, that's the thing I feel worst about actually.
What stops you from saying yes?
The emails.
And if I'm away I'll come back to 200 again.
That might need some time.
So even rest has a price?
Yeah, exactly.
Can't remember the last time I was properly off.
What did you do for yourself before October?
We ran.
10 kilometers every Saturday morning.
We've done it for 6 years.
And now?
I stopped about 2 months ago.
My legs feel like lead.
And I just never went back.
How do you feel about that?
Like I've lost a part of myself.
It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.
What would it mean to get some of that back?
A lot, probably.
You can't picture the time that would come from.
Let's leave that for a moment.
What is your relationship with your boss like?
Pearson.
He's alright as a person, but he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
What do you do when one arrives?
I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm not bad. Claire hates it.
What are you afraid would happen if you didn't answer?
Then he'd think I wasn't committed.
There is a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.
And if they did?
I don't know.
I think part of me would be relieved.
I'd feel horrible about being relieved.
I have a mortgage.
Both things can be true.
I suppose so.
I never said that I would hold.
How are you moves apart from the tiredness?
A lot, mostly.
And irritable.
I slept at a colleague last week who ate nothing and went and sat in the toilets for 10 minutes.
What was happening for you in those minutes?
Her hair was going and my hands were shaking.
I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.
Has it happened before?
Couple of times.
Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.
That sounds frightening.
It was. I hadn't told anyone about it, not even Claire.
Thank you for telling me. What are you afraid it means?
That I'm losing it. That I'm gonna end up like, I don't know, coping.
Have you noticed anything that makes it worse?
Coffee, probably. I want about 6 cups a day. I've started having wine in the evenings to
switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.
How do you feel about the wine?
Easy. It works for an hour. I wake up at 3 anyway. I know it's not helping.
You are noticing that clearly. That is useful.
It doesn't feel useful. Feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.
I hear a person who has been holding a great deal on his own for a long time.
What was it like to say it today?
Strange. Bit of relief actually. Like putting on a bag that I didn't realize I was carrying.
What do you carry when you would like to put down first?
The nights, I think.
If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.
We can start here.
Tell me a thing about your family growing up.
Shape how you handle this.
My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire.
He never complained about anything.
Not once.
That's the same.
Just get on with it.
And you?
I'm the same.
I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.
What would you say to him if he were here?
That I'm not weak.
Just very tired.
That sounds like something you could say to yourself as well.
Maybe.
I don't know if I believe it yet.
That's fine.
You don't have to.
Let's think about what we could do between now and next week.
Would you be willing to try something small?
Depends how small.
Can't get much left.
Very small.
I'll fix time in the evening when you switch off your phone.
Even for 20 minutes.
Beers don't hate that.
what would actually happen in 20 minutes?
I think probably you wouldn't even notice.
Would you try it?
Yeah, half past nine, perhaps.
I could make it a dangles glare.
Do you have a sofa?
That sounds good.
And a note of how the night goes?
I can do that.
right down when I wake up
if I wake up
we're nearly out of time
how are you feeling right now?
tired
but lighter
it's normal to feel
a bit shaky after saying all that
very normal
it takes energy to say it loud
loud
right, thank you
I think I needed to hear that
same time next week?
Yeah, I'll be here.
I'll try to make it on time.
The trains are awful.
